question.text: A mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> attached to free end of a spring executes SHM with a period of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. If the mass is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> the period of oscillation increases by one second, the value of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is ________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Time period of oscillation is given by T=2πmk, where k is the force constant of the spring. 

∵ Spring is same, therefore, spring constant will be same.

Putting the different values,

In the first case          T=1=2πmk

In the second case    T'=2=2πm+3k

 Dividing the equations, we get

 TT'=12=mm+3

⇒mm+3=14⇒4m=m+3⇒m=1

Thus, m=1 kg
